name: Saint Joseph of Cupertino
history: A Franciscan friar of southern Italy, so slow at his books and clumsy at his work that he was sent away by one order and barely accepted by another. Ordained priest, he was caught up in ecstasy so often, and was seen by so many witnesses to rise from the ground in prayer, that he was kept away from crowds. He is a patron of students.
life: Joseph Desa was born in 1603 at Copertino in Apulia, in a shed, it is said, because his father’s debts had cost the family their home. A sickly, absent-minded boy, he was nicknamed Boccaperta, open-mouth. The Capuchins took him as a lay brother but sent him away after eight months for his clumsiness. The Conventual Franciscans at La Grottella accepted him to look after their mule, and his humility and prayer won him a place in the novitiate. He struggled with study, and tradition tells that at each examination he was questioned only on the one text he knew well; he was ordained in 1628. His ecstasies, in which he was seen to rise into the air, drew such crowds that the Inquisition examined him, and he was moved from friary to friary, ending at Osimo, where he died in 1663. He was canonised in 1767.
prayerTo: Saint Joseph of Cupertino, you were thought a fool and found your joy in God alone. Pray for all students, especially those who struggle and fear failure, and for me, that I may do my best with the gifts I have, accept my limits with humility, and let my heart be lifted to God in prayer. Amen.
penance: Do a humble task today that you would normally leave to others, and pray for a student facing exams.
meditation: Joseph had little learning but a great love for God. Do you trust that God values your love more than your achievements?
prayer: O God, Who willed that all things be drawn unto Your Son when He was raised above the earth, mercifully grant, by the merits and example of Your seraphic Confessor Joseph, that, having been raised above all earthly desires, we may be found worthy to come unto Him. Who livest…
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
